I analyzed the issue with the "next submitter" link in exercise/staff_views.py. The problem was that the NextUnassessedSubmitterView was not correctly identifying which students need manual assessment according to the requirements specified in the GitHub issue.

The key insight from the issue is: "A student should be considered manually graded once any one of his/her submissions has been manually graded. The 'next submitter' link should not repeat a student who has been manually graded."

I implemented a fix that:
1. Identifies all submitters who have submitted to the exercise
2. Excludes those who have ANY graded submissions in this exercise (since they've already been manually graded)
3. Orders the remaining submitters by ID for deterministic selection
4. Implements proper round-robin navigation using the 'prev' parameter
5. Redirects to the submission list when all students have been assessed

The fix ensures that students are excluded from the next submitter list as soon as ANY of their submissions receives manual grading, preventing the repetition of already-graded students and properly terminating when all students have completed manual assessment.

I implemented a fix for the NextUnassessedSubmitterView in exercise/staff_views.py that correctly identifies students who need manual assessment. The fix ensures that a student is considered to need assessment only if NONE of their submissions in the exercise have been graded (i.e., they have zero graded submissions). This prevents students who have already received manual grading on any submission from appearing in the next submitter list, addressing all three issues mentioned in the GitHub issue: 1) not repeating students graded on non-latest submissions, 2) not repeating already-inspected students when others need grading, and 3) properly terminating when all students have completed manual assessment.
